clean_source_blocks.text: President Trump has concluded a two-day visit to Beijing at a high-stakes summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. The US leader hailed the trip as a success, saying he had struck "fantastic trade deals", but little detail is known about the discussions. Neither side has announced any major trade breakthroughs or business deals. The BBC's China correspondent Laura Bicker has this analysis. The French president stood up during a conference in Kenya to tell the audience to quieten down, saying it was “impossible” for speakers to be heard. The Dutch foreign ministry confirmed that a British, German and Dutch national had now been taken from the virus-hit ship. Each bear in the installation in Washington, DC, is meant to represent one of the children Ukraine says have been abducted by Russia.
President Trump has concluded a two-day visit to Beijing at a high-stakes summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

The president’s two-day summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping saw praise and claims of progress from both sides, but also persistent differences on Taiwan and other key issues. When it came to Iran, the U.S. may have touted agreement but Beijing appeared to give Trump the bare minimum, according to one analyst. Beijing’s agreement to keep the Strait of Hormuz open and its statement that Iran should not obtain nuclear weapons cost China “very little,” said Craig Singleton, a senior fellow and China expert at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies. “Those rhetorical commitments cost China very little,” Singleton said in emailed comments. “The harder test is whether Beijing pressures Tehran, curbs Chinese purchases of Iranian oil, or helps Washington turn general language into observable outcomes."

President Trump wrapped up his whirlwind three-day trip to China after tea and lunch with Xi Jinping early Friday, Eastern time. The commander-in-chief and his Chinese counterpart discussed a wide range of pressing issues over the course of the historic summit, aimed at shoring up relations between Washington and Beijing and opening up the Communist country to American businesses. Here are the top takeaways from Trump’s trip: Xi raised the issue of Taiwan with Trump right out of the gate, but the president has thus far refused to budge on changing the longstanding US policy toward the self-governing, democratic island that China claims as its own.

[Lähde: New York Post]
President Trump wrapped up his whirlwind three-day trip to China after tea and lunch with Xi Jinping early Friday, Eastern time.

The commander-in-chief and his Chinese counterpart discussed a wide range of pressing issues over the course of the historic summit, aimed at shoring up relations between Washington and Beijing and opening up the Communist country to American businesses.

Here are the top takeaways from Trump’s trip:

Xi raised the issue of Taiwan with Trump right out of the gate, but the president has thus far refused to budge on changing the longstanding US policy toward the self-governing, democratic island that China claims as its own.

“President Xi stressed to President Trump that the Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning wrote on X Wednesday. “If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. Otherwise, the two countries will have clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy.

“‘Taiwan independence’ and cross-Strait peace are as irreconcilable as fire and water.”

Mao’s statement concluded with a quote from the meeting attributed to Xi: “Safeguarding peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait is the biggest common denominator between China and the US.”

Since the late 1970s, the US “One China” policy has acknowledged Beijing’s claim to the island and avoided directly advocating for Taiwanese sovereignty.

In an interview with “NBC Nightly News with Tom Llamas,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio insisted Xi’s protests had no effect.

“US policy on the issue of Taiwan is unchanged as of today and as of the meeting that we had here today,” he said. “It was raised. They always raise it on their side. We always make clear our position and we move on to the other topics.”

The two heads of state appeared to have found common ground on Iran — with Xi even offering to assist Trump in the region, according to the US president.

“President Xi would like to see a deal made, he would, he would like to see a deal made. And he did offer. He said, ‘If I can be of any help at all, I would like to be of help,’” Trump told Fox News’ Sean Hannity.

“Anybody that buys that much oil has obviously got some kind of a relationship with him,” Trump added. “He’d like to see the Hormuz Strait open. He said, ‘If I could be of any help whatsoever, I would like to help.’”

payload.title: Trumpin Kiinan-vierailu päättyi ilman ilmoitettuja kauppaläpimurtoja
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump tapasi Kiinan presidentin Xi Jinpingin Pekingissä korkean panoksen huippukokouksessa. Trump kuvasi matkaa onnistuneeksi, mutta julkisuuteen ei ole kerrottu merkittävistä kaupan läpimurroista tai suurista yrityssopimuksista.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump on päättänyt Kiinan-vierailunsa, jonka aikana hän tapasi Kiinan presidentin Xi Jinpingin Pekingissä korkean panoksen huippukokouksessa. Trump kuvasi matkaa onnistuneeksi ja sanoi saavuttaneensa “fantastisia kauppasopimuksia”, mutta julkisuuteen ei ole kerrottu yksityiskohtia merkittävistä kaupan läpimurroista tai suurista yrityssopimuksista.

## Paljon myönteisiä arvioita, vähän konkreettisia tietoja

Lähdeaineiston mukaan tapaaminen oli osa yritystä vakauttaa Washingtonin ja Pekingin suhteita sekä avata Kiinaa laajemmin amerikkalaisille yrityksille. Sekä Yhdysvaltojen että Kiinan puolelta esitettiin myönteisiä arvioita ja väitteitä edistyksestä, mutta julkinen näyttö jäi niukaksi. Kumpikaan osapuoli ei ole ilmoittanut sellaisista suurista kauppa- tai liiketoimintaratkaisuista, jotka vahvistaisivat Trumpin kuvauksen konkreettisiksi tuloksiksi.

Vierailun tulkinta jää siksi avoimeksi. Johtajien kasvokkainen tapaaminen voi itsessään olla diplomaattisesti merkittävä, koska maiden suhteita ovat painaneet useat kiistakysymykset. Samalla vaikutuksia on vaikea arvioida, kun sopimusten sisällöstä, aikatauluista tai toimeenpanosta ei ole annettu tarkkoja tietoja.

## Taiwan nousi esiin heti keskusteluissa

Keskusteluissa nousi esiin Taiwan, jota Kiina pitää omana alueenaan. Lähdeaineiston mukaan Xi nosti Taiwanin esille heti tapaamisen alussa, mutta Trump ei ole muuttanut Yhdysvaltojen pitkäaikaista linjaa itsehallinnollista ja demokraattista saarta kohtaan. Tämä viittaa siihen, ettei yksi Yhdysvaltojen ja Kiinan suhteiden herkimmistä kysymyksistä ratkennut huippukokouksessa.

## Iran-kirjaukset jäivät käytännön testiin

Myös Irania koskevat keskustelut jäivät tulkinnanvaraisiksi. Yhdysvallat voi kuvata Kiinan kannanottoja edistysaskeleiksi, mutta asiantuntija Craig Singletonin mukaan Pekingin lupaukset Hormuzinsalmen avoinna pitämisestä ja Iranin ydinaseiden vastustamisesta maksavat Kiinalle hyvin vähän. Hänen mukaansa todellinen testi on se, painostaako Peking Teherania, rajoittaako se iranilaisen öljyn ostoja tai auttaako se muuttamaan yleiset kirjaukset havaittaviksi toimiksi.

Vierailun jälkeen keskeinen kysymys on, muuttuuko johtajien myönteinen puhe käytännön päätöksiksi. Toistaiseksi julkinen tieto viittaa enemmän diplomaattiseen avaukseen kuin selkeään sopimuspakettiin.
summary_bullets: Trump tapasi Xi Jinpingin Pekingissä korkean panoksen huippukokouksessa.
Trump kuvasi vierailua onnistuneeksi, mutta suuria kauppa- tai yrityssopimuksia ei ole ilmoitettu.
Taiwan ja Iran jäivät keskustelujen perusteella edelleen avoimiksi kiistakysymyksiksi.
payload.journalist_note: Lähdeaineisto tukee ydintä Trumpin ja Xin tapaamisesta, niukoista julkisista yksityiskohdista sekä Taiwanin ja Iranin kaltaisista avoimista kysymyksistä. Aineistossa on ristiriita vierailun kestosta, joten artikkelissa vältetään täsmällistä kestoväitettä.

When it came to Iran, the U.S. may have touted agreement but Beijing appeared to give Trump the bare minimum, according to one analyst. Beijing’s agreement to keep the Strait of Hormuz open and its statement that Iran should not obtain nuclear weapons cost China “very little,” said Craig Singleton, a senior fellow and China expert at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies. “Those rhetorical commitments cost China very little,” Singleton said in emailed comments. “The harder test is whether Beijing pressures Tehran, curbs Chinese purchases of Iranian oil, or helps Washington turn general language into observable outcomes."

President Trump wrapped up his whirlwind three-day trip to China after tea and lunch with Xi Jinping early Friday, Eastern time. The commander-in-chief and his Chinese counterpart discussed a wide range of pressing issues over the course of the historic summit, aimed at shoring up relations between Washington and Beijing and opening up the Communist country to American businesses. Here are the top takeaways from Trump’s trip: Xi raised the issue of Taiwan with Trump right out of the gate, but the president has thus far refused to budge on changing the longstanding US policy toward the self-governing, democratic island that China claims as its own.
